name: Lady Borrid and Murkin's Army
tagline: Ancient coppices of hazel and chestnut. North-south paths are trampled with bootprints.

procedural.encounter_notes: Military patrols from Murkin's Army are common on the forest paths.

entries.description: A patrol of 1d4+1 soldiers (mixed humans and shorthorns) marching in formation. They demand to know the party's business and may attempt press-ganging.
Lady Borrid and 1d4 hunting companions tracking game through the woods. She is courteous to travelers who do not impede her hunt.
Roll on standard High Wold encounter table

procedural.foraging_results: Successful foraging yields hazelnuts (1d6 portions), chestnuts (1d4 portions), or forest mushrooms (1d4 portions, 1-in-6 chance of mild hallucination if not properly prepared)

investigation_hazard.description: Sneaking near or investigating Murkin's Army camp risks discovery. There is a 3-in-6 chance sentries spot the party and raise the alarm.

description: Ancient coppices of hazel and chestnut. North-south paths are trampled with bootprints.

points_of_interest.name: Lady Borrid's Hunting Lodge
points_of_interest.description: Among the thickets of blackthorn in the north of the hex is a small, high-gabled brick manor, replete with pointed turrets and balconies surveying the woods.
points_of_interest.tagline: A hunter's retreat filled with trophies of legendary beasts
points_of_interest.entering: An unlocked front door engraved with hunting motifs leads to a wood-panelled hall, at the far end of which hangs a mighty moose head. Entering without permission causes the moose head to bellow, alerting all within to the intrusion.
points_of_interest.interior: Feasting hall with plush, ivy-carved wooden furnishings and decked with the taxidermied heads, horns, and antlers of a multitude of fearsome beasts, including a manticore's head, an antler wraith's antlers, and a 5′ wide wyrm's skull with the inscription 'The Wyrm of Odd.' Upper floor has bedroom suites furnished in a luxurious but modest style.
points_of_interest.exploring: The lodge has three floors: the ground floor feasting hall and kitchens, the upper floor bedchambers, and cellars below. A careful search of the trophy room reveals the Horn of Blasting among the mounted horns. The cellars contain wine stores and a concealed vault.
points_of_interest.leaving: Lady Borrid sees guests off personally if they depart on good terms. Those who leave by stealth may be tracked by Brynne, her giant weasel companion.
points_of_interest.inhabitants: Lady Borrid, her animal companion Brynne—a white-furred giant weasel (DMB—unfailingly loyal to Lady Borrid, does not check Morale), and 1d6 hunting companions (Level 1 hunters—DMB).

roll_tables.name: Hunting Companions Present
roll_tables.description: Roll to determine which hunting companions are at the lodge

entries.title: Empty Lodge
entries.description: Lady Borrid is out hunting with all companions. Only servants remain. The lodge is lightly guarded.

entries.title: Recovering Hunter
entries.description: One injured companion rests by the fire, nursing a wound from a recent hunt. They speak freely of Lady Borrid's activities.

entries.title: Preparing for Hunt
entries.description: Lady Borrid and 1d4 companions prepare weapons and provisions for an expedition. They may invite skilled-looking travelers to join.

entries.title: Celebrating a Kill
entries.description: A successful hunt is being celebrated with wine and song. Lady Borrid is in excellent spirits and generous to visitors.

entries.title: Taxidermy Session
entries.description: Lady Borrid oversees the mounting of a fresh trophy. She speaks at length of the creature's powers and the hunt's dangers.

entries.title: Strategy Meeting
entries.description: Lady Borrid and her companions study maps and discuss the 'cheese monstrosity' of Dwelmfurgh. Serious mood; interruptions unwelcome.

roll_tables.name: Trophy Room Curiosities
roll_tables.description: Notable items among the hunting trophies (one per visit)

entries.title: The Wyrm of Odd
entries.description: A 5-foot-wide skull of a blood wyrm, with the inscription 'The Wyrm of Odd.' Lady Borrid slew this beast in her youth, earning her fame throughout Dolmenwood.

entries.title: Manticore Head
entries.description: A fearsome manticore's head, jaws frozen in a snarl. The eyes seem to follow visitors. Some claim it still speaks prophecy on moonless nights.

entries.title: Antler Wraith Rack
entries.description: The ethereal-seeming antlers of an antler wraith, mounted in silver. They glow faintly in darkness and feel cold to the touch.

entries.title: Horn of Blasting
entries.description: Among the mounted horns, an unassuming bronze horn that is actually a Horn of Blasting (p407). Lady Borrid considers it a mere curiosity.
entries.mechanical_effect: Horn of Blasting can be obtained

entries.title: Painted Hunting Scenes
entries.description: A series of paintings depicting Lady Borrid's greatest hunts. One shows Lord Murkin as a young man, before he grew cruel. She rarely speaks of it.

entries.title: Map of Dwelmfurgh
entries.description: A detailed map showing the central reaches of Dwelmfurgh, with a location marked 'Cheese Thing?' Lady Borrid's next quarry.

special_features: Horn of Blasting concealed among trophies
Magical moose head alarm: bellows when unauthorized entry occurs
Secret chamber in cellars with vault containing chalices and jewels worth 8,000gp, a Fairy Shortbow carved from a giant antler, and a quiver of 12 Fairy Arrows (Breggle Bane)
secrets: Secret door in the cellars leads to a vault containing chalices and jewels worth 8,000gp, a Fairy Shortbow (p412) carved from a giant antler, and a quiver of 12 Fairy Arrows (Breggle Bane, p412)
The moose head alarm can be silenced by feeding it acorns—known only to Lady Borrid and her closest companions

evening_hazard.description: If visitors have made a favorable impression, Lady Borrid invites them to dine with her. This is both an honor and an opportunity for conversation.

alerts.description: The mounted moose head at the end of the hall bellows loudly when unauthorized visitors enter, alerting Lady Borrid and all inhabitants.
alerts.bypass_method: Feed it acorns to silence it

concealed_items.name: Horn of Blasting
concealed_items.description: An unassuming bronze horn hidden among the mounted trophy horns. Only a careful examination reveals its magical nature.

concealed_items.name: Secret Vault Door
concealed_items.description: A concealed stone door in the cellar wall, cunningly disguised as part of the masonry. Close inspection reveals faint seams and a hidden latch mechanism.

locks.description: A concealed door in the cellar wall leads to a hidden vault. The door is disguised as part of the stone wall.

sub_locations.name: Trophy Room
sub_locations.description: The main feasting hall lined with mounted heads, horns, and antlers from Lady Borrid's legendary hunts.

sub_locations.name: Cellars
sub_locations.description: Wine stores and provisions beneath the lodge. A concealed vault lies behind one wall.

sub_locations.name: Secret Vault
sub_locations.description: A hidden chamber containing the Borrid family treasures and documents.

entry_conditions.description: Entering without permission triggers the moose head alarm. Polite visitors are welcomed by Lady Borrid if she is present.

outcomes.success: Lady Borrid welcomes the visitors and offers refreshments
outcomes.failure: Visitors are politely but firmly asked to leave
outcomes.hostile: Brynne the giant weasel is commanded to drive out the intruders

points_of_interest.name: Murkin's Army
points_of_interest.description: In a secluded dell in the south of the hex, a mile into the woods, can be found a ring of canvas tents, sloppily camouflaged with sprays of bracken and oak. Clustered to one side are tables, log stools, barrels of pickled turnips and eggs, and racks of hanging squirrels and rabbits.
points_of_interest.tagline: A sullen military camp of press-ganged soldiers and scheming knights
points_of_interest.entering: Visitors are challenged by sentries at the camp perimeter. Those who identify themselves are brought before Sergeant Snidebleat for questioning, then brusquely told to move along. Sneaking in requires avoiding the 2d4 sentries posted around the dell.
points_of_interest.interior: The camp consists of 12 canvas tents arranged in a rough circle around a central fire pit. Snidebleat's command tent is larger and set apart. A supply area holds barrels of pickled provisions and racks of hunted game. A makeshift training ground features straw dummies and pike racks.
points_of_interest.exploring: Exploring the camp openly is forbidden—Snidebleat will have intruders escorted out or arrested. Sneaking reveals low morale among troops, whispered complaints about Lord Murkin, and the location of pressed recruits held under guard.
points_of_interest.leaving: Visitors are escorted to the edge of the dell by two soldiers. Those who were arrested are released at the hex border with a warning. Press-ganged recruits who escape face pursuit.
points_of_interest.inhabitants: 18 shorthorns (DMB) and 22 humans (Level 1 fighters—DMB) under the command of the longhorn Sergeant Snidebleat. The troops' morale is low, many of them having been press-ganged into service.

roll_tables.name: Camp Activities
roll_tables.description: What's happening at the camp when PCs arrive

entries.title: Pike Drill
entries.description: Soldiers train with pikes under Snidebleat's critical eye. She berates them for sloppiness while clearly bored.

entries.title: Mess Time
entries.description: Soldiers eat from the constantly steaming stew pot. Complaints about the food (and everything else) are audible.

entries.title: Press-Gang Returns
entries.description: A patrol returns with 1d4 new 'recruits,' peasants seized from nearby hexes. They're being processed into the ranks.

entries.title: Formation March
entries.description: The entire camp is marching in formation around the dell. Snidebleat rides a mule, shouting orders.
entries.mechanical_effect: Camp is mobile; harder to sneak in

entries.title: Furtive Drinking
entries.description: Many soldiers have found ale and are drinking furtively. Discipline is lax. Snidebleat is in her tent.

entries.title: Inspection Day
entries.description: An emissary from Lord Murkin inspects the troops. Everyone is on their best behavior. Snidebleat barely conceals her contempt.

roll_tables.name: Soldier Morale
roll_tables.description: The current mood of the troops

entries.title: Near Mutiny
entries.description: Whispered talk of desertion or uprising. One wrong move could spark violence.
entries.mechanical_effect: Soldiers may be recruited against Murkin

entries.title: Deeply Resentful
entries.description: Sullen compliance. Soldiers obey orders but do the minimum. Open grumbling.

entries.title: Resigned
entries.description: Soldiers have accepted their fate. They follow orders mechanically without complaint or enthusiasm.

entries.title: Cautiously Hopeful
entries.description: Rumors of pay increases or the war ending soon have lifted spirits slightly.

entries.title: Drunk and Rowdy
entries.description: Someone smuggled in ale. Soldiers are loud and potentially aggressive.

entries.title: Fresh Victory
entries.description: A successful skirmish or capture has bolstered morale. Soldiers are unusually cooperative.

special_features: Pike training ground with straw dummies
Constantly steaming pot of stew (dubious quality)
Prisoner holding area for press-gang recruits
secrets: Most soldiers would desert if given the chance and guaranteed safety
Snidebleat keeps a hidden cache of her personal wealth (20 onyxes worth 50gp each) buried beneath her tent

evening_hazard.description: Staying near the camp at night risks encountering a patrol of 1d4 soldiers checking the perimeter.

alerts.description: Sentries spot intruders and raise the alarm. 2d4 soldiers respond within minutes.
alerts.bypass_method: Successful stealth check to avoid 2d4 sentries

concealed_items.name: Sergeant Snidebleat's Onyxes
concealed_items.description: A pouch of 20 polished onyx gems buried beneath Snidebleat's command tent. Her escape fund.

sub_locations.name: Command Tent
sub_locations.description: Snidebleat's larger tent set apart from the others. Contains maps, orders, and her personal effects.

sub_locations.name: Prisoner Holding Area
sub_locations.description: A roped-off section where press-ganged recruits are held under guard before being 'processed' into the army.

sub_locations.name: Supply Area
sub_locations.description: Barrels of pickled provisions and racks of hunted game. The constantly steaming stew pot sits here.

sub_locations.name: Training Ground
sub_locations.description: A makeshift area with straw dummies and pike racks where soldiers drill.

entry_conditions.description: Visitors are challenged by sentries and brought before Sergeant Snidebleat for questioning.

outcomes.success: Visitors are brusquely told to move along after questioning
outcomes.failure: Visitors are escorted out of the camp with a warning
outcomes.hostile: Visitors are arrested and held for Lord Murkin's judgment

variable.description: sentries on patrol around the dell

points_of_interest.name: Lady Borrid's Hidden Vault
points_of_interest.description: A hidden chamber behind a secret door in the cellars of Lady Borrid's Hunting Lodge. The vault contains the Borrid family treasures: chalices and jewels worth 8,000gp, a Fairy Shortbow carved from a giant antler, and a quiver of 12 Fairy Arrows (Breggle Bane). Ancient family documents are also stored here.
points_of_interest.tagline: A secret treasure chamber containing Borrid family heirlooms
points_of_interest.entering: The secret door swings open silently on well-oiled hinges, revealing a small stone chamber lit by the faint glow of magical preservation wards.
points_of_interest.interior: A 10-foot square chamber with stone shelves lining the walls. Silver chalices and loose gemstones glitter on one shelf. A giant antler bow rests in a wooden rack, accompanied by a quiver of arrows that shimmer with fey enchantment. A locked ironbound chest contains family documents.
points_of_interest.exploring: The treasures are openly displayed for anyone who finds this chamber. The locked chest contains legal documents regarding land inheritance and letters between Borrid family members.
points_of_interest.leaving: The secret door can be closed from inside or outside, returning the chamber to its hidden state.
special_features: Magical preservation wards keep the contents in pristine condition
secrets: The documents in the chest prove Lord Murkin's father intended a more equitable division of lands, which could legally challenge Simeone's rule

npcs.name: Lady Amonie Borrid
npcs.title: Level 9 Hunter
npcs.description: A limber human woman in her 50s, with arched brows, chestnut eyes, and a blonde braid down her back. Dresses in a green woollen tunic and brown leather breeches. While she spent her youth roaming the deep woods, avoiding political matters, Borrid now follows the manoeuvrings of the High Wold noble houses with concern. She is famed throughout Dolmenwood for having slain a mighty blood wyrm that terrorised Odd.
desires: To turn back the tides of war in the High Wold
Views Lord Ramius (p65) as potential peacemaker
possessions: A cloak of autumnal leaves (grants +2 AC)

known_topics.content: Lady Borrid rises gracefully, her hand resting on the giant weasel at her side. 'Travelers in my woods are always welcome, provided they come in peace. Brynne here will tell me if you don't.' The weasel's eyes glitter intelligently.

Her eyes light up. 'The hunt is life itself—the patience, the tracking, the moment of confrontation. I've stalked antler wraiths through frozen mists and cornered a manticore in its lair. The forest has no secrets from a true hunter.'

She gestures to the massive skull on the wall. 'The Wyrm of Odd. Thirty years ago, it terrorized the village, taking livestock and children. I tracked it for three months through Dwelmfurgh before I found its lair. That was the fight of my life.'

Her expression clouds. 'Simeone is my cousin, yes. We were close as children—before his father died and bitterness consumed him. I barely recognize the man he's become. Cruel, grasping, obsessed with conquest.'

'This war with Nodlock will destroy us all. Simeone cannot see that even victory would leave the High Wold weakened. And if he turns his soldiers on the common folk...' She shakes her head. 'Someone must broker peace.'

'Lord Ramius of Everdusk understands balance. He protects Nodlock from Simeone's aggression—not out of love, but wisdom. If anyone can bring the longhorn lords to reason, it is he. I've written to him, but received no reply.'

'These woods I know better than my own lodge. Every deer trail, every badger sett. The hazel coppices are ancient—older than any human settlement. Walk carefully and listen; the forest speaks to those who attend.'
She strokes the giant weasel's fur. 'Brynne has been with me for twelve years. I found her as a kit, abandoned after hunters killed her mother. She's saved my life more times than I can count.'

'My next hunt takes me north, to central Dwelmfurgh. There are tales of a... cheese monstrosity? It sounds absurd, but hunters have vanished. Whatever it is, I intend to find it.' A gleam enters her eye.
'The longhorn lords squabble like children while the real threats—the Drune, the creatures of the deep wood—go unchecked. I stay out of politics, but politics will not stay out of these woods.'

secret_info.content: Lady Borrid secretly sympathizes with the rebellion against her cousin. She has never met Timilda Brumble, but approves of the Cabbage Plot as a peaceful form of resistance that may draw Duke Brackenwold's attention.
secret_info.hint: She speaks of 'the troubles in Murkin's domain' with a hint of satisfaction rather than concern.

secret_info.content: Timilda Brumble has sent messages to Lady Borrid through trusted travelers, asking for her support. Borrid has not replied directly but has allowed her lodge to be used as a waypoint for those fleeing Murkin's soldiers.
secret_info.hint: She asks pointed questions about travelers' origins and seems unsurprised by news from hex 0108.

secret_info.content: Borrid has been quietly working to arrange a meeting between Lord Ramius and representatives of House Nodlock, hoping to create a united front against Murkin before he starts a war. The meeting would be held at her lodge.
secret_info.hint: She has been preparing extra guest chambers and speaks of 'important visitors expected soon.'

secret_info.content: The secret vault in her cellars contains not just wealth but also family documents proving Murkin's father intended a more equitable division of lands. This could be used to legally challenge Simeone's rule.
secret_info.hint: When discussing her cellar, she hesitates and changes the subject.

relationships.description: Maternal cousin of Lord Simeone Murkin. They were close as children but have grown apart due to his cruelty.
relationships.notes: Borrid disapproves of Murkin but maintains minimal contact

relationships.description: Has received messages from Timilda regarding the rebellion. Quietly supports the cause without direct involvement.
Snidebleat commands the army in this hex. Borrid views her with wary respect—a dangerous woman with her own agenda.
Borrid sees Lord Ramius as the only noble capable of brokering peace. She has written to him seeking an audience.

faction_profile.notes: Cousin to Lord Murkin but opposes his policies. Maintains formal ties while working quietly against his war plans.

npcs.name: Sergeant Crewwin Snidebleat
npcs.title: Level 4 Knight
npcs.description: A longhorn woman with russet fur, amber eyes, and 2′-long, outward curving horns. Dresses in burnished plate mail with a full visor helm. Snidebleat is a member of Lord Murkin's (p65) knightly retinue, the Horns of Kolstoke. Her loyalty is bought—she loathes Murkin and his pompous schemes.
desires: Ascent to a position of aristocracy and wealth
Assistance in brokering a potential alliance with Red Gwen (hex 0311) to accomplish said goals
secrets: She loathes Murkin and his pompous schemes
possessions: A Ring of Energy Resistance (Fire, p410), searing to the touch

known_topics.content: She looks down her long muzzle at you. 'State your business. This is Lord Murkin's camp—the army that will soon crush House Nodlock. Unauthorized visitors are... unwelcome.'
'We train. We drill. We wait for Lord Murkin to decide the time is right.' Her tone suggests she finds this tedious. 'The glory of battle awaits—eventually.'
'Forty soldiers. Shorthorns and humans, pressed into service or bought with promises of plunder. They're adequate.' Her dismissiveness suggests she thinks them barely sufficient.
'Lord Murkin dreams of conquest. Nodlock Castle, then the High Wold entire.' She sounds bored. 'Grand ambitions for a half-breed with more chin-locks than sense.'
'House Nodlock is weak, protected only by Lord Ramius's favor. When that protection fails—and it will—we march. A week's campaign at most.'
'I am of the Horns of Kolstoke—Murkin's personal retinue. Twelve longhorn knights, the finest warriors in his service.' Pride flickers briefly before returning to boredom.
'I serve where glory awaits. When this war is won, there will be lands and titles to distribute. I intend to claim my share—and more.'
'The hunter? She keeps to her lodge, playing with her pets and trophies. A waste of noble blood. She could be a power in the High Wold if she chose.'
Her ears prick up. 'Red Gwen? The bandit queen of hex 0311?' She pauses carefully. 'I've heard she commands considerable forces. Interesting.'

secret_info.content: Snidebleat genuinely despises Lord Murkin. She finds him pompous, cruel, and incompetent. She serves only because the position offers opportunity for personal advancement.
secret_info.hint: Her praise of Murkin is always delivered in a flat, perfunctory tone. She never uses his name with respect.

secret_info.content: For sufficient gold (100gp), Snidebleat will allow travelers to pass through the camp unmolested, 'forget' to report suspicious activities, or provide information about Murkin's plans.
secret_info.hint: She eyes valuable equipment and jewelry with calculating interest.

secret_info.content: Snidebleat has been secretly corresponding with Red Gwen, proposing an alliance. She believes that with the bandit queen's forces, she could carve out her own domain when the war weakens both Murkin and Nodlock.
secret_info.hint: She asks too many questions about the roads south and seems interested in anyone who has traveled from hex 0311.

secret_info.content: The army's morale is dangerously low. Many soldiers were press-ganged and would desert given the opportunity. A few words in the right ears could spark mass desertion or even mutiny.
secret_info.hint: She seems unconcerned about discipline issues, as if expecting the army to fall apart anyway.

secret_info.content: Snidebleat has buried her personal wealth (the 20 onyxes worth 1,000gp total) beneath her command tent. She plans to flee with it if the war turns against Murkin.
secret_info.hint: She never leaves camp for long and always returns to check her tent first.

relationships.description: Serves Lord Murkin as a knight of the Horns of Kolstoke. Privately loathes him.
Has been secretly corresponding with Red Gwen about a potential alliance.
Maintains polite distance from Lady Borrid. Respects her hunting prowess but considers her politically naive.
Commands the 40 soldiers at the camp. Views them as tools rather than people.

faction_profile.notes: Member of the Horns of Kolstoke. Loyalty is purchased, not genuine. Secretly plotting her own advancement.

secrets: Lady Borrid secretly sympathizes with the rebellion in hex 0108 and has allowed her lodge to shelter those fleeing Murkin's soldiers
The army's morale is dangerously low; most soldiers were press-ganged and would desert if given safe passage
Sergeant Snidebleat is in secret correspondence with Red Gwen (hex 0311), planning to establish her own domain after the war
Lady Borrid's cellar contains a hidden vault with treasure and legal documents that could challenge Murkin's rule
Lady Borrid is attempting to arrange a peace summit between Lord Ramius and House Nodlock at her lodge
dm_notes: Making ready for the hunt: Borrid and her companions are preparing to venture north to hunt down the cheese monstrosity rumoured to lair in central Dwelmfurgh (see hex 0405). Friendly PCs may be invited to join the hunt. Activities at Murkin's Army: Mustering for war against House Nodlock (see Human Nobility, p56). For now, this consists mainly of pike training, marching in formation, and furtive swilling of ale. Key plot hooks: (1) PCs can help Lady Borrid hunt the cheese monstrosity; (2) PCs can infiltrate the camp and free press-ganged prisoners; (3) PCs can broker between Borrid and the rebellion in 0108; (4) PCs can be hired by Snidebleat to carry messages to Red Gwen; (5) PCs can discover the vault documents and use them politically.
